issues.detail: Error handling is limited to a brief note on stuck managed resources; it omits provider install failures, missing Function dependencies, XR composition errors, deletion policies, and credential rotation.

Example 1 relies on an XBucket XRD and Composition that are never shown (only described as 'same shape as XDatabase'), and Example 2 is just a few debug commands, so the examples are not fully runnable or realistic end to end.
The Secret manifest uses AWS's documented placeholder example keys (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE), and the Guidelines explicitly warn against committing real credentials.

scenarios.name: namespaced-queue-abstraction
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric: Namespaced scope, required size enum, engine enum, no claimNames, Pipeline with function-patch-and-transform and a map transform from size to instance class, and a direct namespaced XDatabase. A uses function-go-templating with dict lookups instead of patch-and-transform and a map transform, and makes engine required but not size, so it misses key rubric items despite a correct XRD scope and direct XR.

scenarios.name: debug-stuck-managed-resource
scenarios.rationale: B hits every rubric item (kubectl get managed, describe bucket, the events field-selector command, and the missing ProviderConfig and IAM-permission causes), while A skips the events command and only touches the credentials cause in a table of many causes.

scenarios.name: install-and-configure-aws-provider
scenarios.rationale: Both install Crossplane via Helm into crossplane-system, pin providers (though both use placeholders or unverified versions, A with a concrete v2.8.2 tag), create a Secret and a default ProviderConfig with source: Secret and secretRef, and warn against committing credentials. B adds a stronger production-safety treatment (IRSA, deletion policies, etc.) and mentions External Secrets/SOPS for keeping secrets out of git, while A only says to keep the secret out of git and to use an external secrets operator in passing, so B edges ahead on the secrets-manager suggestion.
